messages:
sam: Quick sync — we need to finalize the headroom commitments playbook for Dedicated pools before next week's launch. Who's got objections to a simple SLA-first approach?
anya: No objections, but we should be explicit about signals: CPU/GPU util, queue latency, and failing start attempts.
mike: Agreed. For first cut I recommend a deterministic headroom layer + an emergency burst bucket. Keep autoscale conservative.
dean: Customers are asking for committed burst credits they can buy/renew monthly. Need clarity: does burst consume reserve or separate quota?
kira: From CS: enterprise customers want predictability. They prefer a small committed buffer they can guarantee for business peaks.
anya: Proposal: two-layer model — reserved (committed) + burst (best-effort). Reserved is backed by contract. Burst is throttleable and billed differently.
sam: That aligns with earlier notes. Need concrete launch criteria though: what counts as "works"?
mike: Minimal launch criteria: 1) enforceable reservation mapping to tenant, 2) observable metrics (usage, throttles, latency), 3) safe fallback to hosted variant when preempted.
anya: Also: rollout controls — canary by account tier, and kill-switch for perf regressions.
ops-bot: deploy: a/dedicated-headroom-v1 scheduled for canary on prod-dedicated-us-west on 2026-05-12 04:00 UTC
dean: Pricing ops: suggest burst billed at 2x reserved rate but with daily caps. We can iterate after pilot.
kira: For customer comms, we need an api contract example and sample UI copy for console. I'll draft a short FAQ.
sam: Technical spec question — who owns the reservation enforcement? runtime or control plane?
anya: Enforcement at runtime is simplest for hard limits. Control plane for assignment + audits. So split responsibilities.
mike: I'll prototype a runtime token-bucket keyed by "reservation-id". Simple pseudocode:
```
if reservation_tokens >= req_cost:
  consume(reservation_tokens)
else if burst_tokens >= req_cost && burst_enabled:
  consume(burst_tokens)
else:
  reject(429)
```
This makes preemption deterministic.
sam: Nice. What about autoscale interaction? If pool scales up, reserved should remain untouched. Burst should only be consumed when the pool is saturated.
anya: Right — scale-up should be triggered on sustained queue latency or high p95. But we must avoid oscillation; add cooldown and governor.
dean: From contract side, need SLA wording: "reserved capacity available 99.9% of time, subject to scheduled maintenance" and clear definitions of "available" vs "provisioned".
kira: Also logging + audit trail for when reservations are preempted and which fallbacks applied. Customers will ask.
mike: Observability checklist: per-reservation throughput, preempt_count, latency_p50/95/99, burst_consumed, fallback_events. All visible in Console.
sam: Launch readiness checklist draft:
- spec approved (product + eng + infra)
- canary deploy + smoke tests
- billing rule in place for burst/reserved
- docs + FAQ + console UI mock
- monitor runbooks and oncall playbook
Anyone object to these items?
anya: No, add: load test that simulates noisy neighbors + tenancy spikes.
ops-bot: perf-test: dedicated-headroom-load-10k scheduled (estimate 6h)
dean: For customers on Dedicated beta, propose a 30-day pilot with options to convert burst into reserved after 30d if usage warrants.
kira: Good idea — we'll offer conversion guidance and recommend commit sizes based on 30d p95.
sam: Ok next steps: Mike to spike token-bucket runtime and sketch metrics emitters; Anya to write rollout gating and cooldown; Dean/Kira to draft commercial terms and pilot offer. We'll reconvene Thurs 11am PT.
anya: I'll put the rollout gating doc in the product folder and tag everyone.
mike: Spike started, will post notes by EOD.
nana: (typo) — meant to say +1 to all the above :thumbsup:
